# parse-check -- a STUB parent project, for CI only. Never build what it
# generates, and never use it as a template for consuming MscsUnitTests.
#
# ../../../CMakeLists.txt is a SUBDIRECTORY script, not a project. It is
# normally pulled in by add_subdirectory() from the MSCS solution root, and it
# expects four library targets to already exist -- msgcore, targetcore,
# p2pplatform and treefs -- which live in sibling directories that are not part
# of this repository. Three of those (Platform, P2PeerUtilityHubs, DspChain)
# have no remote at all and TreeFs is on a private non-GitHub host, so a CI job
# that builds the real suite is not merely unwritten, it is not currently
# possible. See tools/hooks/README.md.
#
# This file supplies the three things the subdirectory script assumes of its
# parent -- a project context, the sibling library target names, and the
# _mscs_apply_loader_path() function -- and NOTHING ELSE, so that CI can at
# least run the real CMakeLists.txt through CMake's parser and generator.
#
# WHAT CONFIGURING THIS PROVES
#   * ../../../CMakeLists.txt is syntactically valid CMake, and every command
#     and generator expression in it evaluates for a real generator.
#   * Every source file it names exists at the path it names. CMake errors at
#     generate time on a missing source ("Cannot find source file"), so a test
#     registered against a file nobody added is caught here -- which is the
#     defect class this repository has actually shipped.
#   * Every add_test() it declares can be generated, so CTestTestfile.cmake is
#     produced and the registered test NAMES can be read back and compared
#     against the executables. The invariants job does exactly that.
#
# WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE -- and this is the important half
#   * NOTHING IS COMPILED OR LINKED. The stub targets below are empty INTERFACE
#     libraries carrying no headers and no import libraries, so the generated
#     project would fail at the first #include of P2Pmsg.h. The CI job
#     deliberately stops after generate.
#   * It therefore says nothing about whether any test compiles, links, runs or
#     passes. Every ctest figure this repository's evidence rests on -- Windows
#     41/41, Linux 44/44 -- is produced by hand on a developer machine and by
#     nothing else. A green tick here must never be read as "the suite passes".
#   * Only the non-WIN32 branch is exercised, because the runner is Linux. The
#     MFC/vcxproj half of this file is covered by the suite-wiring job instead,
#     which reads the .vcxproj directly and needs no compiler.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(MscsUnitTestsParseCheck LANGUAGES CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

# The four sibling targets the subdirectory script links against.
#
# SHARED over an empty INTERFACE library, and the reason is worth recording so
# nobody "simplifies" it back: the real CMakeLists.txt puts the sibling DLL/.so
# directories on each test's PATH via $<TARGET_FILE_DIR:msgcore>, and CMake
# refuses that generator expression on an INTERFACE target -- "Target
# 'msgcore' is not an executable or library" -- at GENERATE time, in three
# places. A stub that cannot carry a file location cannot stand in for a
# library that has one.
#
# They still compile nothing here: the job stops after generate, so this source
# is written to disk and never handed to a compiler.
file(WRITE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/mscs_ci_stub.cpp
     "// Generated by parse-check. Never compiled: CI stops after generate.\n")

# THREE targets, and that is the headline. Before the 2026-08-14 split this list
# also needed treefs and p2putilhubs, because unit_suite compiled the TreeFS,
# replication, blob and P2PeerUtilityHubs suites. Those moved to
# MscsUnitTestsExternal, and what is left links only what Msgcore and Targetcore
# provide -- both of which are published repositories. If a real build job is
# ever added here, this is the list it has to satisfy.
foreach(_stub msgcore targetcore p2pplatform)
    add_library(${_stub} SHARED ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/mscs_ci_stub.cpp)
    set_target_properties(${_stub} PROPERTIES LINKER_LANGUAGE CXX)
endforeach()

enable_testing()

# The third thing the subdirectory script assumes of its parent, and the newest.
# ../../../CMakeLists.txt ends with a call to _mscs_apply_loader_path(), which
# puts the sibling DLL/.so directories on each registered test's PATH. That
# function moved to the MSCS solution root on 2026-09-04 -- deliberately, because
# it is needed by every directory that registers a test against msgcore or
# targetcore and P2PeerWeb could not reach the file it used to live in. The root
# is not part of THIS repository, so without the stub below CMake stops at
# "Unknown CMake command" and nothing downstream of it is parsed at all.
#
# A NO-OP IS THE HONEST STUB HERE, and the reason is the reason parse-check
# exists: this job stops after generate and runs no test, so a test environment
# it never reads is not a thing this file can be wrong about. Copying the real
# body would be worse -- two definitions that can drift, with CI checking the
# copy and every build using the original.
#
# WHAT THIS COSTS, stated so nobody reads the tick as wider than it is: the real
# function's own generate-time behaviour -- the $<TARGET_FILE_DIR:...> genex, the
# per-platform variable, its refusal when msgcore/targetcore are absent -- is NOT
# exercised by this job, and cannot be until the solution root is reachable from
# CI. What IS still proved is everything above the call: the subdirectory script
# parses and generates to the end, and the call site itself is syntactically
# reached.
function(_mscs_apply_loader_path)
endfunction()

add_subdirectory(${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../../.. MscsUnitTests)
